title: US National YoYo Contest 2024
content: The 2024 US National Yo-Yo Contest was held June 21–23 at the Sheraton Downtown in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, organized by the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) — bringing together the nation's top qualifiers from regional competitions across the United States. Justin Dauer won his first 1A championship title, while Matt Szeto claimed the 2A national title, Alex Hattori extended his historic streak to ten national championships in the 3A division, Philip White won the 4A division, and John Wolfe secured the 5A championship. The event also saw Bella Freestylin' take first place in the Women's Freestyle division, named Kira Morrow the Over-40 winner, and presented the International division title to Australia's Brandon Vu.

content:

title: Asia Pacific Yo-Yo Championship (AP) 2019
content: The 2019 Asia Pacific Yo-Yo Championship was the final edition of the contest before it went on a multi-year hiatus due to the global COVID-19 pandemic. Garbkamol Limangkul defended his 1A AP title, winning for the second consecutive year, while Japanese competitors heavily dominated the rest of the field, with Arata Imai, Tsubasa Takada, and Yoshihiro Abe taking the 2A, 4A, and 5A titles, respectively. Singapore's own Thawhir Iqbal proudly secured the 3A championship for the host nation. The regional contest would remain paused until its highly anticipated return and rebranding as the global "AP Yo-Yo Open" in 2026.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: Spinworkx
Venue: Singapore
Dates: July 2019
meta.yya_competition_notes: Continental championship serving as a major regional qualifier for international play.

title: Asia Pacific Yo-Yo Championship (AP) 2020
content: There was no Asia Pacific Yo-Yo Championship held in 2020. Following its last edition in 2019, the AP championship entered a multi-year hiatus caused initially by the COVID-19 pandemic. During this time, competitive yo-yo largely shifted to the Online World Yo-Yo Contest (OWYYC). The AP contest finally made its highly anticipated return in March 2026, where it was rebranded as the Asia Pacific (AP) Yo-Yo Open and transitioned into a fully global competition open to players from all countries.

title: Asia Pacific Yo-Yo Open (AP26) 2026
content: The 2026 AP Yo-yo Open was a monumental event for the international throwing community, marking the highly anticipated return of the competition after nearly seven years. Held from March 6 to 8 at the *SCAPE Ground Theatre in Singapore, the contest broke boundaries by allowing global competitors to enter, raising the already elite standard of play. Australia's Allon Chen took home the 1A Championship title in an incredibly stacked finals bracket.

title: California State Yo-Yo Championship 2026
content: The 2026 California State Yo-Yo Contest brought the California throwing community together on April 25 at the Chico Women's Club. As one of the longest-running state yo-yo competitions, the event featured stacked 1A and X-Division flights, alongside heavily populated Futures (amateur) brackets for players 12 & Under and 13 & Over. Shuyun Tang successfully defended his title, putting on a dominant performance in the 1A Finals to win his second consecutive California State Championship. The event was supported by a strong roster of sponsors, including Big Red YoYo Strings, Kendama Co, OneDrop YoYos, and Sol Kendamas.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: National Yo-Yo League (NYYL)
Venue: Chico Women's Club, Chico, California

title: California State Yo-Yo Contest 2025
content:
About the California State Yo-Yo Contest 2025

The 2025 California State Yo-Yo Contest brought competitive yo-yoing back to Downtown Chico's City Plaza for the first time since 2019, drawing competitors across 1A, X Division (2A/4A), and two Futures youth divisions. Organized through the National YoYo League with local coordination by Nate Dailey and the National Yo-Yo Museum, the event capped off with a judges' exhibition freestyle from world champion Gentry Stein.

title: Colorado State Yo-Yo Contest 2026
content:
About the Colorado State Yo-Yo Contest 2026

The 2026 Colorado State Yo-Yo Contest was held on August 23, 2026 at The People's Building in Aurora, Colorado, organized by Todd Rollenhagen of the Mile High YoYo Club under the National Yo-Yo League's sanctioning umbrella. Nine yo-yo divisions were contested: 1A, 0A, X-Division, Sports 1A (split by age 12-and-under and 13-and-up), Sports X, Advanced Youth 1A, a Legacy division for competitors 40 and older, and Doc Lucky's Duos. Christian Harper topped the 26-competitor 1A field, while Myles Gregory won the mixed-style X-Division as a 4A entrant over 2A, 3A, and 5A competitors, and Nathan Irwin posted a perfect 70.00 technical score en route to winning 0A. Organizers reported the 2025 edition roughly doubled both attendance and participant counts over 2024, though no exact 2026 attendance figure has been published.

title: East Japan Yo-Yo Contest (EJ-1) 2025
content:
About the East Japan Yo-Yo Contest (EJ-1) 2025

The East Japan Yo-Yo Contest 2025 Block-1 (EJ-1) was held on March 15, 2025 at Seimei Education and Culture Hall in Higashikurume, Tokyo, presented by Cloud Native Inc. and organized by the Japan Yo-Yo Federation (JYYF). The event served as the first of two Kanto regional qualifier blocks for the 2025 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest, which was held in Yokohama in June. Seven divisions were contested including the standard freestyle categories and a B Division open to beginners and intermediate players. Ryo Igarashi took the 1A title with a score of 93.8, while South Korean competitor Lee Jaehyuk claimed 2nd in 2A — a notable international showing at a domestic regional event. Takato Sasaki won 3A, Tsubasa Takada took 4A honors, and Akira Nishiguchi topped the 5A field.

Presenter: Cloud Native Inc.
Qualifier for: 2025 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest (Yokohama, June 21–22, 2025)

title: European Yoyo Championship (EYYC) 2025
content: The 2025 European Yo-Yo Championship (EYYC) was officially unhosted. Because the 2025 World Yo-Yo Contest took place in Prague, Czech Republic, the Czech Yoyo Association was entirely occupied with organizing the massive world-level event. Since the Polish association had just hosted the EYYC the previous year in 2024, no other European organization had the manpower available to take on the 2025 continental championship. In the absence of the EYYC, organizers focused on newer regional events instead, such as the inaugural Benelux Yoyo Championship. The European Yo-Yo Championship successfully returned the following year, taking place in May 2026 in Bratislava, Slovakia.

meta.yya_competition_notes: Continental championship serving as a major regional qualifier for international play.

title: European Yoyo Championship (EYYC) 2026
content: The 2026 European Yo-Yo Championship was held from May 2 to 3 at the Kamel klub in Bratislava, Slovakia. It gathered competitors from over 16 countries to compete for the prestigious European titles and seeded spots to the World Yo-Yo Contest. The event highlighted the evolving boundaries of yo-yo tricks pushed by young stars like Jakub Dolejš, as well as the enduring skill of veterans in the Royal division.

title: Illinois State Yo-Yo Contest 2024
content:
About the Illinois State Yo-Yo Contest 2024

The 2024 Illinois State Yo-Yo Contest marked the event's return to the Chicago Toy & Game Fair (CHITAG) after an absence, drawing competitors from beginner to professional level across 1A, X-Freestyle, Sport Freestyle, and the family-friendly Doc Lucky's Duos team format. Run by Touch of the North Events in partnership with Doc Lucky's Yo-Yo Talk, it combined competition with CHITAG's broader toy-fair programming.

meta.yya_additional_notes:

Venue: Donald E. Stephens Convention Center, 5555 N River Rd, Rosemont, IL 60018, USA (CHITAG main stage)
Attendance: not officially reported
Specialty awards: Gibb Helping Hands — Jack Hudspath & Miles Gregory; Gibb You Did Awesome — Francisco Yao

title: Illinois State Yo-Yo Contest 2025
content:
About the Illinois State Yo-Yo Contest 2025

Held again on CHITAG's main stage, the 2025 contest split into a Saturday trick-ladder/workshop day and Sunday freestyle finals across 1A, Dual Hand, 4A, and 5A divisions. Presented by Duncan Toys, it debuted a first-ever Kendama Expression Session, signaling the organizer's push to broaden the event beyond yo-yo into the wider skill-toy community.

content:
About the Indiana State Yo-Yo Contest 2025

Held October 4, 2025 at The Irving Theater in Indianapolis, the 2025 Indiana State Yo-Yo Contest revived a state championship that had been inactive since 2013. Run under the National Yo-Yo League banner with organizing support from the NapTown Crew and Joshua Richardson, the one-day event ran four competitive divisions — 1A, 5A, an X Division covering 2A/3A/4A styles, and a beginner-friendly Sport Division.

title: Indiana State Yo-Yo Contest 2026
content:
About the Indiana State Yo-Yo Contest 2026

The 2026 Indiana State Yo-Yo Contest took place September 19, 2026 at The Irving Theater in Indianapolis, run on the National Yo-Yo League's contest platform. Isaac Viteri won the 1A division with an 88.50 final score, ahead of Zion Wilson (60.17) and Connor Pflueger (56.73), in a field of 18. John Datoy swept the advanced styles, winning both 5A (70.35) and X-Division (66.66) with Brandon Cole second in 5A and William Smith (2A) second in X-Division. Sports 1A was split by age: Noah Leung won Ages 12 & Under with 86.00, and Baxter Woiwode edged Joash Kaufman 65.23 to 65.21 for Ages 13 & Up. A Sport Ladder also ran with six competitors; the official results page lists only its freestyle order, with no published placements.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: not stated on results page; sanctioned via National Yo-Yo League (NYYL)
Venue: The Irving Theater, 5505 E Washington St, Indianapolis, IN 46219, USA
Attendance: 18 in 1A, 5 in 5A, 4 in X-Division, 5 in Sports 1A (12 & Under), 7 in Sports 1A (13 & Up), 6 in Sport Ladder (freestyle order only, no placements published)
meta.yya_competition_notes: Isaac Viteri won the 1A state title with an 88.50, and John Datoy took both 5A and X-Division.

title: Japan National Yo-Yo Contest 2025
content: The 2025 Japan National Yo-Yo Contest (JN25) was held at the Yokohama Education Center Sunrise Hall in Yokohama, Kanagawa, Japan. Serving as the 27th edition of the prestigious national championship, this year notably introduced the International Open Freestyle (IOF) division, which allowed non-Japanese competitors to officially take the JN stage. Throughout the event, Japan's top throwers battled to claim national titles and secure seeded spots for the 2025 World Yo-Yo Contest in Prague, Czech Republic.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: Japan Yo-Yo Federation (JYYF)
Venue: Yokohama Education Center Sunrise Hall, Yokohama, Kanagawa, Japan
Dates: June 21–22, 2025

title: Midwest Regional Yo-Yo Championship (MWR) 2026
content:
About the Midwest Regional Yo-Yo Championship (MWR) 2026

The Midwest Regional Yo-Yo Championship is one of the National Yo-Yo League's flagship regional contests, held each spring at the Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota. The event traces back to an inaugural 1998 contest, and Dave "Dazzling Dave" Schulte is listed as its organizer and head judge. The 2026 edition ran May 30 on the mall's Huntington Bank Rotunda center stage, across Beginner's Luck, Sport, and Championship (1A and X-style) divisions. Hunter Feuerstein won the Championship 1A title, and Josh Kanoff (competing in 4A) topped the Championship X division. As with other NYYL regionals, the top-placing eligible U.S. resident earns an automatic finals seed to the U.S. Nationals, with the next four finishers receiving semifinal seeds.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: Dave "Dazzling Dave" Schulte (organizer/head judge; inaugural contest held 1998)
Venue: Mall of America, Huntington Bank Rotunda, 60 E Broadway, Bloomington, MN 55425, USA
Attendance: not verified for 2026 (2025 edition reported 63 competitors from 11 states)
Divisions run: Beginner's Luck, Sport Ladder, Sport 1A, Sport X, Championship 1A, Championship X
Note: full placements for Beginner's Luck, Sport Ladder, Sport 1A, and Sport X, plus 2nd-5th order for Championship 1A, were not extractable — official results are hosted in a JS-rendered widget at compete.yoyocontest.com/results/2026-midwest-regionals. Only the Championship 1A winner and semifinalist list, and the Championship X winner, were confirmed via the official Nationals qualification page.
meta.yya_competition_notes: Annual NYYL regional contest held on the Mall of America's center stage in Bloomington, MN, since 1998. Hunter Feuerstein won Championship 1A and Josh Kanoff (4A) took Championship X in 2026.

yya_location.address: Mall of America, Huntington Bank Rotunda, 60 E Broadway, Bloomington, MN 55425, USA

title: Minnesota State Yo-Yo Contest 2026
content:
About the Minnesota State Yo-Yo Contest 2026

The 2026 Minnesota State Yo-Yo Contest took place October 4, 2026 at the Underground Music Venue in Minneapolis, hosted by the MN State Yo-Yo Club and run through the National Yo-Yo League's contest platform. Adrian Velez won the 1A division with a 95.00 final score, ahead of Zion Wilson (71.50) and Jethro Chen (65.12). In X-Division, open to 2A through 5A stylists, Tyson Engelke (4A) won with 89.00 over Tyler Ostby (5A) and Ramir Aguilos (5A). Colin Cloyd took Sports 1A with 83.33, followed by Bennett Scholl and Cole Richtsmeier. The day also included a Doc Lucky's Duos division and a Kendama freestyle showcase; the official results page lists only freestyle order for those, with no published placements.

title: New York State Yo-Yo Contest 2023
content:
About the New York State Yo-Yo Contest 2023

The New York State Yo-Yo Contest is the flagship annual event of the New York Yo-Yo Club (NYYYC), held at Coney Island USA's historic sideshow theater. The 2023 edition drew competitors across 1A, 2A, X-Division, and Amateur divisions, with Nick de Valpine topping the 16-player 1A field. Judging was led by the Scales Collective under head judge Colin Beckford.

content:

Now in its fifth year, the New York State Yo-Yo Contest returned to Coney Island USA on October 5, 2024, selling out its competitor slots. Chandler Steele topped a 19-player 1A field; Colin Beckford and Ryan Connolly took the Dual X and Aerial X titles respectively; Tey Chang won Amateur. Luke Trautwein, who finished 5th overall, was separately awarded the eligible "NY State Champion" residency title.

title: Pacific Northwest Regional (PNWR) 2024
content:
About the Pacific Northwest Regional (PNWR) 2024

The Pacific Northwest Regional Yo-Yo Championship 2024 was held on February 24, 2024 at Seattle Center Armory in Seattle, Washington — the final edition of the event at its historic Seattle home after nearly two decades. Organized by the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) under longtime contest director Nathan Crissey, the event drew 59 registered competitors and served as a qualifier for the National Yo-Yo Contest. Hunter Feuerstein claimed his second consecutive PNWR 1A title over a 41-person field, a result that previewed his third-place finish at the 2024 World Yo-Yo Contest later that year. Justin Dauer placed second and went on to win the 2024 US National Yo-Yo Championship. The X Division saw Jared Marcus take the overall title with a 5A performance, with Christopher Chunn placing second in 4A.

title: Pacific Northwest Regional (PNWR) 2025
content:
About the Pacific Northwest Regional (PNWR) 2025

The Pacific Northwest Regional Yo-Yo Championship 2025 was held on March 29, 2025 at the McMenamins Crystal Ballroom in Portland, Oregon — the first time in the event's history it left Seattle for a Portland venue. Organized by the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL), the event served as the opening regional qualifier of the season for the National Yo-Yo Contest held in Las Vegas that summer. Hunter Feuerstein won the 1A championship for an unprecedented third consecutive year, besting a field of 16 finalists that included multiple World Championship veterans. Matt Szeto took the X Division title in 2A, Aliyah Tan placed second with a 3A performance, and Royce Pinzon rounded out the 4A field. Sport 1A divisions were contested across four age brackets, and division winners earned NYYL qualification seeds for the national finals.

title: Return Yoyo Cup 2026
content: The 2026 Return Yoyo Cup took place on January 10 at the Songhae Arthall in Seoul, Republic of Korea. Supported heavily by title sponsor yoyorecreation, the contest featured a highly competitive 1A division that saw top international talent going head-to-head. The event also featured guest demonstrations from world-class players like Tony Šec, Takumi Yasumoto, Eom Gun Ju, Hajime Miura, and Kim Min Joon. Lin Jun Yi ultimately secured the 1A Championship title.

Title Sponsor: yoyorecreation (who fully sponsored the venue costs this year)

title: Rocky Mountain Regional (RMR) 2024
content:
About the Rocky Mountain Regional (RMR) 2024

The 2024 Rocky Mountain Regional was the first-ever running of this National Yo-Yo League regional event, hosted at the Holiday Inn Denver East in partnership with the Denver-based Mile High Yo-Yo Club. Eventual 1A champion Justin Dauer edged out Kris Toledo and Marc Zuno for the title, and went on to claim the US National 1A Championship later that year.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: National Yo-Yo League (NYYL), in partnership with the Mile High Yo-Yo Club
Venue: Holiday Inn Denver East, 3333 Quebec Street, Denver, CO 80207, USA
Attendance: not reported (21 entered 1A prelims, 15 advanced to finals)
Note: this was the inaugural RMR — no 2023 edition existed, and RMR was skipped entirely in 2025 (schedule/cost cited informally, resumed 2026). The published results source lists only 1A.
meta.yya_competition_notes: The inaugural Rocky Mountain Regional Yo-Yo Championship, held in Denver, launched the NYYL's newest regional stop; Justin Dauer's 1A win preceded his US National title later that season.

title: Rocky Mountain Regional (RMR) 2026
content: The 2026 Rocky Mountain Regional Yo-Yo Championship took place on May 16 at the Denver Marriott Westminster in Colorado. Organized by the National Yo-Yo League, the event invited competitors and spectators of all ages to celebrate the Rocky Mountain throwing scene. In the highly competitive 1A division, Marc Zuno successfully secured the 1st place spot to become the Regional Champion.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: National Yo-Yo League (NYYL)
Date: May 16, 2026
Venue: Denver Marriott Westminster, Westminster, CO, 80021
Attendance: 55 competitors (300+ total event attendance per Denver Gazette)
meta.yya_competition_notes: Regional qualifier providing pathway to national championship. Winners advance with seeds to nationals.

title: San Diego Classic Yoyo Contest 2024
content:
About the San Diego Classic Yoyo Contest 2024

The first San Diego Classic Yoyo Contest ran January 27, 2024, at Queen Bee's Art & Cultural Center in San Diego's North Park neighborhood, drawing competitors across 1A Pro, 1A Sports, and a multi-style X Division. Justin Dauer topped a deep 1A Pro field, Jace Sanchez won 1A Sports, and Matt Szeto took the X Division. It followed NYYL/IYYF judging standards while operating as an independently run contest.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: independently run (San Diego yoyo community, @sd.yyc), following NYYL/IYYF scoring standards but not an NYYL-sanctioned state or regional qualifier
Venue: Queen Bee's Art & Cultural Center, 3925 Ohio Street, San Diego, CA 92104, USA
Attendance: not reported; ticket price range $5-30
Note: this was the inaugural (1st annual) edition.
meta.yya_competition_notes: The inaugural San Diego Classic drew a deep 1A Pro field at Queen Bee's Art & Cultural Center, won by Justin Dauer.

yya_location.address: 3925 Ohio Street, San Diego, CA 92104, USA

title: San Diego Classic Yoyo Contest 2025
content:
About the San Diego Classic Yoyo Contest 2025

Returning to Queen Bee's Arts and Cultural Center on May 3, 2025, the 2nd Annual San Diego Classic expanded its 1A Sport field to 19 competitors and again ran 1A Pro and a mixed-style X Division. Kris Toledo won 1A Pro with a maxed-out technical score, Matt Szeto repeated as X Division champion, and 1A Sport ended in a first-place tie between Daniel Legge and Geo Gan.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: independently run, Eventbrite lists Alec Cecena as organizer
Venue: Queen Bee's Arts and Cultural Center, 3925 Ohio St, San Diego, CA 92104, USA
Attendance: not reported; spectator pass required
Note: dead-even tie for 1st in 1A Sport (Daniel Legge & Geo Gan, both 98.4/100).
meta.yya_competition_notes: The 2nd Annual San Diego Classic saw Kris Toledo take 1A Pro and a rare co-championship crown 1A Sport.

title: Texas State Yo-Yo Contest 2008
content:
About the Texas State Yo-Yo Contest 2008

The 2008 Texas State Yo-Yo Contest is believed to be the first edition organized by Travis Owen, who described 2010 as his "third time" running the contest. Neither the exact date nor the venue for the 2008 edition could be independently confirmed: a single source places the contest in the Dallas area, but the confirmed 2009 and 2010 editions were both held in Austin, TX (Jester Auditorium, University of Texas), casting doubt on the Dallas location for 2008. No division results survive in any public record for this year.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: Travis Owen (inferred from his 2010 blog post calling that year his "third time" running the contest, implying 2008 was his first year; not independently dated)
Venue: UNCONFIRMED. A single wiki source states the contest was held in the Dallas area; however the confirmed 2009 and 2010 editions were both in Austin, TX (Jester Auditorium, UT Austin), which conflicts with the Dallas claim.
Attendance and division placements: not found in any surviving public record.
meta.yya_competition_notes: Earliest known edition of Travis Owen's Texas State Yo-Yo Contest; exact date and venue unconfirmed, and the "Dallas area" location conflicts with the confirmed Austin, TX venue of the 2009/2010 editions.

title: US National YoYo Contest 2019
content: The 2019 US National Yo-Yo Championship was held on Sunday, July 7th at the Independence Seaport Museum in Philadelphia. This marked the continuation of the contest's migration around the country after moving from Chicago in 2018. Gentry Stein secured his fourth US National 1A title, while Alex Hattori, Ryan Connolly, and John Wolfe continued to establish their dominance in their respective multi-yo-yo and counterweight divisions. The event was heavily supported by sponsors such as YoYoExpert, Duncan Toys, C3yoyodesign, and YoYoFriends.

title: US National YoYo Contest 2020
content: The 2020 US National Yo-Yo Contest was officially cancelled due to the global COVID-19 pandemic. The National Yo-Yo League (NYYL), prioritizing the health and safety of the yo-yo community during the height of the crisis, made the difficult decision to completely pause the 2020 competition season. Consequently, no US National Champions were crowned for 2020.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: National Yo-Yo League (NYYL)
Venue: Cancelled
Dates: Cancelled
meta.yya_competition_notes: Note: The cancellation of the 2020 US National Yo-Yo Contest marked an unprecedented hiatus for the event, which had run continuously since its inception in 1993. The pandemic also forced the cancellation of the 2021 US National Yo-Yo Contest. The competition finally made its return as an in-person event two years later, taking place in Mesa, Arizona, in June 2022.

title: US National YoYo Contest 2021
content: The 2021 US National Yo-Yo Contest was officially cancelled due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. Following the cancellation of the 2020 event for the same reason, the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) opted to keep the competition on hiatus to ensure the safety of players and attendees. As a result, no US National Champions were crowned for the 2021 season.

meta.yya_additional_notes:
Organizer: National Yo-Yo League (NYYL)
Venue: Cancelled
Dates: Cancelled
meta.yya_competition_notes: Note: Because of the pandemic, the NYYL officially cancelled both the 2020 and 2021 US National events. While the international yo-yo scene saw the creation of the Online World Yo-Yo Contest (OWYYC) in 2021 to allow players to compete virtually, the official US National competition remained completely paused. The contest eventually made its in-person return the following year, taking place in June 2022 in Mesa, Arizona.

title: US National YoYo Contest 2022
content: The 2022 US National Yo-Yo Contest marked the triumphant return of in-person national competition after the 2020 and 2021 contests were canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Evan Nagao claimed his third US National 1A title, while Alex Hattori continued his dominance in 3A. The event featured a wide array of sponsors, including Duncan Toys, YoYoFactory, CLYW, and YoYoExpert.

title: US National Yo-Yo Contest 2025
content:
About the US National Yo-Yo Contest 2025

The 2025 US National Yo-Yo Contest was held June 27–29 at the Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino in Las Vegas, Nevada, organized by the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) — the first edition held at this venue after the contest's long association with Chico, California, where it was founded in 1993. Connor Seals won the 1A championship title, while Matt Szeto claimed a second consecutive 2A national title, Jared Marcus secured his third national championship in 5A, and Ryan Connolly won the 4A division. The event also presented the Donald F. Duncan Family Award for Industry Excellence to Mark Diehr, the National Achievement Award to Dave Adams, and named Hunter Feuerstein the Most Inspirational Player.

title: US National Yo-Yo Contest 2026
content:
About the US National Yo-Yo Contest 2026

The 2026 National Yo-Yo Contest, organized by the National Yo-Yo League, ran June 26–28 at the Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino following a season of nine sanctioned regional qualifiers. Sixteen-year-old Thomas Rajan of Madison, Alabama took his first 1A national title, edging runner-up Chandler Steele (who posted a rare perfect 10.00 originality score) and third-place Hunter Feuerstein — the win earns Rajan a US seed at the 2026 World Yo-Yo Contest in Japan. Other division champions included Matt Szeto (2A), Aliyah Tan (3A), Ryan Connolly (4A, edging Josiah Pulsifer by just 0.52 points), Sterling Quinn (5A), Katie Thompson (Women's), and Park Jun Sang of South Korea (1A International), part of a field drawing competitors from Korea, Singapore, Mexico, Canada, Brazil, and Japan.

title: United Yoyo Contest (UYYC) 2026
content:
About the United Yoyo Contest (UYYC) 2026

The United Yoyo & Kendama Contest (UYYC 26) took place June 6, 2026 at the Missouri History Museum in St. Louis, Missouri, timed to coincide with National YoYo Day. Born from a 2016 merger of the Kansas State and Missouri State (MoYo States) yo-yo championships, UYYC has grown into a multi-discipline state-championship event spanning 1A, X, Sport (12 & Under and 13 & Over), and Over 40 yo-yo divisions alongside kendama freestyle and ladder competitions and a chess side tournament. Thomas Rajan (AL) claimed his second consecutive 1A title, while Mike Marshall (KS) and Brandon Cole (MO) topped the X Division as their respective states' champions. Event Director Christopher Ananda, who founded MoYo States in 2006 and joined with Blake Freeman's Kansas State contest in 2016 to form UYYC, continues to run the event.

title: Virginia State Yo-Yo Contest 2026
content:
About the Virginia State Yo-Yo Contest 2026

The 2026 Virginia State Yo-Yo Contest (VSYC-26) was held September 19, 2026 in Center Court at Dulles Town Center in Sterling, Virginia. Organized by the DMV Throwers Yo-Yo & Skill Toy Club and presented by Goodles, it used the National Yo-Yo League (NYYL) ruleset, with results published on Compete.YoYoContest.com. The event had 53 registered competitors from 14 states, ages 7 to 38, of whom 50 competed, with an organizer estimate of 200 to 500 spectators. Divisions were X, 1A and Sport/Beginner/Junior. Chandler Steele (OH) won X Division with 91.00, Ryan Kim (MD) won 1A with 95.50, and Steen Harty (GA), age 12, won Sport/Beginner/Junior with 74.03. Virginia State Champion titles, awarded to the top Virginia resident in each division, went to Alex Curfman (X), Bryant Baus (1A) and Christian Eustace (Sport/Beginner/Junior).

title: World YoYo Contest 2012
content: The 2012 World Yo-Yo Contest was held at the Rosen Plaza Hotel in Orlando, Florida. Hiroyuki Suzuki claimed his final 1A World Champion title, scoring 83.51 points. Japanese competitors swept many of the divisions with victories from Shu Takada (2A), Rei Iwakura (4A), and Takeshi Matsuura (5A). Hank Freeman secured the 3A title for the United States, earning an 88.65. The event also notably hosted a long sleeper world record attempt, where Simpson Wong achieved a sleep record of 30 minutes 28.30 seconds using the C3yoyodesign BTH.

title: World YoYo Contest 2013
content: The 2013 World Yo-Yo Contest was a historic transition year for the sport. It marked the end of the event's long-running tenure in Orlando under Gregory Cohen and served as the first official IYYF World Championship before the contest began rotating globally. In the 1A division, János Karancz made history by becoming the first European to win the World Title. This was also the first and only time the 1A top-three podium featured no players from Japan or the United States. Furthermore, Takeshi Matsuura secured his fifth World Title in 5A with a near-perfect score of 95.1.

title: World YoYo Contest 2014
content: The 2014 World Yo-Yo Contest marked a historic milestone for the sport as management officially transferred to the newly formed IYYF, and the event was hosted outside the United States for the first time in twenty-two years. Gathering over 1,000 players and fans from more than 30 countries, the contest saw Gentry Stein claim the highly coveted 1A World Champion title. Japanese competitors swept the remaining championship playstyles with victories from Takuma Yamamoto (2A), Hajime Miura (3A), Rei Iwakura (4A), and Takeshi Matsuura (5A), while Tessa Piccillo secured the Women's 1A title.

title: World YoYo Contest 2015
content: The 2015 World Yo-Yo Contest was a landmark event for the sport, marking the first time the modern World Contest was held outside of Europe or the United States (initiating the IYYF's Europe/Asia/Americas rotation). Zach Gormley secured the highly coveted 1A World Champion title in what commentators called one of the most competitive and stacked finals in yo-yo history. Shinji Saito extended his legendary record by winning the 2A title, bringing his World Championship count to an incredible 13.

title: World YoYo Contest 2016
content: The 2016 World Yo-Yo Contest took place from August 4 to 7 in Cleveland, Ohio, marking the competition's major return to the United States. Sanctioned by the International Yo-Yo Federation (IYYF), the massive event gathered over 1,000 yo-yo players and fans from more than 20 countries at the Renaissance Cleveland Hotel. In the highly competitive 1A division, Shion Araya secured his first World Champion title. The year also featured absolute dominance from Japanese throwers across all main playstyles, sweeping the championship divisions with victories by Shu Takada (2A), Hajime Miura (3A), Rei Iwakura (4A), and Takeshi Matsuura (5A).

title: World YoYo Contest 2020
content: The 2020 World Yo-Yo Contest was originally scheduled to take place in Budapest, Hungary. However, due to the global COVID-19 pandemic, the event was postponed and ultimately canceled entirely. The International Yo-Yo Federation (IYYF) and the local organizing team faced significant financial losses from non-refundable venue deposits and travel arrangements; the IYYF ultimately absorbed these costs to support the Hungarian organizers. Because the entire contest was canceled, no World Yo-Yo Champion titles were awarded for the year 2020.The cancellation of the 2020 event marked an unprecedented pause in the modern competitive yo-yo circuit. To maintain the spirit of global competition during the ongoing lockdowns, the IYYF shifted to a digital format, creating the "Online World Yo-Yo Contest" (OWYYC) which took its place for the 2021 and 2022 seasons. The official, in-person World Yo-Yo Contest did not return until 2023 when it was held in Osaka, Japan.

The digital format allowed competitors from all over the world to submit their freestyles via video, keeping the spirit of the international yo-yo community alive during a period of global lockdowns and travel restrictions.

title: World YoYo Contest 2000
content:
About the World YoYo Contest 2000

The 2000 World Yo-Yo Contest was held July 8-9, 2000 at Nickelodeon Studios at Universal Studios, Universal Orlando in Orlando, Florida, with Harvey Lowe as guest of honor. Divisions were A, AA, X and Teams plus an S (Sport) division, and the event hosted the first World Peg Top Contest. Yu Kawada (Japan) won A with a freestyle score of 93.17 ahead of Hidemasa Semba and Matthew Rose; Tomoya Kitamura won AA ahead of Koji Yokoyama and Masahiro Tanikawa; Hironori Mii won X ahead of Takahiko Hasegawa and Brian Roberts. Nickelodeon aired coverage in August 2000 and National Geographic World planned a February 2001 feature. Team, S and Top results exist on the official site but were not retrieved.

title: World YoYo Contest 2025
content:
About the World YoYo Contest 2025

The 2025 World YoYo Contest was held August 7–10 at Centrum Cubex in Prague, Czech Republic — the second time the city hosted the event, following 2014 — drawing over 300 competitors from 43 countries under the organization of IYYF. South Korea's Mir Kim claimed his third consecutive 1A title, becoming only the second player in history to win three or more 1A World Championships after Hiroyuki Suzuki's four-peat (2004–2006, 2012). Japan's Hajime Miura secured his eighth 3A world title — the most in any single division — while Miri Kim took a third consecutive Women's Freestyle crown and Rei Iwakura earned both the Grand Prix and Entertainment Award in Artistic Performance.

title: World YoYo Contest 2026
content:
About the World YoYo Contest 2026

The 2026 World YoYo Contest ran August 13–16 at Arcrea HIMEJI in Himeji, Hyogo, Japan, organized by the IYYF with the Japan Yo-Yo Federation hosting locally. South Korea's Mir Kim won 1A for a fourth straight year (2023–2026), posting a 98.1 — the widest winning margin of the 1A final, nearly five points over runner-up Jakub Doleš (93.1) and third-place Hunter Feuerstein (93.0). Chun Hay Chan (2A), Tomoya Kurita (3A), Koyo Hashimoto (4A), Jihoo Lee (5A), and Yuzuki Takenaga (Women's Freestyle) took the other championship titles, while Masakazu Yamasaki and Yo-Yo Store REWIND TE earned the Artistic and Entertainment Awards in Art & Performance.
